chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about four men who testified against a woman for adultery, one of whom was her husband. He said: 'Their testimony is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is the husband's testimony valid when he testifies with three other men against his wife for adultery?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the husband’s testimony is fully valid when included among the four witnesses required for *zina*, resolving potential debates about his dual role as accuser and witness. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the husband’s presence does not invalidate the testimony, provided the other conditions of witnesshood are met. It highlights the precision of Imami fiqh in distinguishing between the husband’s unique right to *li'an* and his capacity to serve as a standard witness in the presence of three others.
